transcript:
HEADER
Date: 2026-08-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jon Ortiz (Redwood SE); Samir Rao (CTO, Hydra), Priya Menon (Platform Lead), Liam Chen (Finops), Nora Velasquez (Security)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto): Quick economics run-through, got clear ask for TCO spreadsheet and a technical follow-up re: VPC + KMS.

---
00:00 Samir (Hydra): Okay, thanks everyone for joining, appreciate your time. We wanted this session to be a mix of cost digging and routing options, so we can figure out whether we go hosted first or plan dedicated/reserved for Q4.
00:12 Evelyn (Redwood): Awesome, thanks Samir. Quick intros and then we can jump into your current stack and numbers. I'm Evelyn, AE, Maya's our systems lead today.
00:18 Maya (Redwood): hey, hi, hi. I'll probably ask most of the nitty gritty — batching, cache, and perf tradeoffs.
00:24 Priya (Hydra): Priya here. We're building a design-assist feature inside our SaaS product, interactive chat-plus-generation, target latency ~200-250ms p95 for short prompts, occasionally longer for synthesis tasks.
00:36 Liam (Hydra): Liam from finance, I'm mainly looking at per-token burn and how we can cap monthly spend while sustaining 1000-2k daily active users initially.
00:45 Nora (Hydra): Nora, security. KMS integration, audit logs and residency are must-haves. SOC2 also in our procurement checklist.
00:52 Jon (Redwood): quick note — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. Each has cost and operational tradeoffs; we'll sketch those relative to your workload.
01:05 Samir: rough numbers: expected 250k tokens/day initially ramping to 2-3M tokens/day by month 3 if the pilot goes well. Mix of short prompts (50-200 tokens) and long synth (800-2,000 tokens) maybe 1 in 20.
01:22 Maya: okay that distribution is helpful. For short prompts we often recommend smaller model variants or lower precision quantized variants to cut per-token cost; for long synths we look at batching + KV cache to avoid re-sending prefixes.
01:35 Priya: can you explain KV cache and prefix caching again — we've seen those terms but want to understand practical savings.
01:42 Maya: sure. Prefix caching (auto prefix cache) stores repeated system prompt and context so the runtime doesn't re-tokenize and re-run full compute for the same prefix. KV cache stores transformer past-key-values between tokens during a session so subsequent tokens are generated cheaper and faster — reduces per-token compute for long contexts. In practice, if you have a lot of repeated parts (system messages, boilerplate), prefix cache can cut 10-30% of tokens shipped. KV cache reduces GPU work during generation.
02:10 Samir: and batching — that's grouping multiple requests to fill the GPU efficiently, right? Does that add latency?
02:18 Maya: yes, continuous batching groups concurrent requests; it adds a small scheduling delay (batch window) but can massively reduce per-token cost. Redwood's runtime adapts batch windows based on latency SLOs — for a tight 200ms p95, we keep windows small and favor latency. For cost-first workloads we open windows a bit to increase throughput.
02:38 Liam: can you quantify savings? ballpark per-token?
02:42 Maya: ballpark: hosted per-token on a large open model variant might be $0.0009 - $0.002 per token depending on model and quantization. With batching + prefix caching you often see 20-60% effective savings. Dedicated reserved capacity can further lower core compute cost 30-50% vs hosted list. But dedicated has commit and base monthly cost.
03:05 Samir: so dedicated cheaper per token but we pay for idle/reserved capacity?
03:09 Jon: correct, reserved pools give predictability. If you can commit to a baseline throughput we size pools and show you a monthly TCO. Burst capacity covers spiky loads but is more expensive when used.
03:20 Priya: what's typical pilot approach? Hosted then shift to dedicated?
03:24 Evelyn: yes many customers start hosted to iterate on prompts and UX, then move to dedicated when they need predictable throughput or lower unit cost. Some with regulatory needs start private/VPC from day one.
03:33 Nora: about private — what's the network pattern? we require traffic to stay in our VPC, HSM-backed KMS, and strict egress controls. Can Redwood support that?
03:41 Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane in a VPC; KMS/HSM integrations are supported, plus audit logs. For on-prem we can run a package that talks to your HSM. We'll need to schedule a technical session to walk through firewall rules and service endpoints.
03:58 Liam: ok, for finance, what levers do we control? model choice, quantization, batching window, caching, routing to cheaper variants?
04:06 Maya: all of those. Also token slicing for long responses (streaming partial outputs) and routing policies — for example route cheaper requests to low-cost model variants and latency critical to dedicated/hosted low-latency pools.
04:20 Samir: give an example cost scenario — say 1M tokens/day mostly short prompts, with occasional long ones. Hosted vs dedicated?
04:29 Maya: rough sketch: hosted (mixed model): maybe $900 - $1,800/day depending on model choices; dedicated with moderate reserved pool could be $550-$1,100/day equivalent once amortized, plus monthly reserved fee. Again depends on quantization and caching. We'll run numbers with your exact profile.
04:51 Liam: those ranges are wide; we'll need firm TCO. also curious about sample TPS numbers for threads — we expect bursts at peak (say 200 qps for short prompts) and sustained 20 qps otherwise.
05:05 Maya: for that pattern continuous batching is effective. For 200 qps peaks we rely on burst or extra replicas. Dedicated pools can be autoscaled a bit but reserved capacity gives anchor. We'll simulate with your traffic CSV.
05:18 Priya: any SLA on latency? our UX team will insist on p95 < 250ms for chat.
05:24 Jon: Redwood Dedicated offers SLA-backed latency targets for committed capacity; hosted endpoints are high-perf but SLA depends on plan. We can map that in the TCO doc.
05:33 Nora: security checklist — SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, data retention, audit logs, KMS. Are those baked in?
05:40 Maya: Yes. Hosted has enterprise features including RBAC and audit logs; dedicated and private give more control. KMS/HSM integrations are supported for private; hosted supports customer-managed keys to the extent allowed by cloud providers.
05:53 Samir: procurement will want to see a matrix — what's included in hosted vs dedicated vs private.
05:58 Evelyn: we'll include a features + cost + timeline matrix in the follow-up.
06:02 Liam: billing model — per-token only or spot GPU charges too?
06:07 Jon: hosted is mostly per-token and embeddings/requests. Dedicated has a mix: reserved capacity (flat) + per-token for burst overage, or model-change fees depending on variants. We'll show an amortized effective per-token price.
06:19 Priya: talk me through an example of routing — say we have latency-critical and background summarization tasks.
06:25 Maya: you can set route rules: high-priority traffic goes to dedicated low-latency pool, background summarization routes to cheaper quantized variants in hosted cheaper model families. If dedicated is saturated, we auto-fallback to hosted cheaper variants — can be policy-controlled.
06:40 Samir: what about output quality regression when you move to quantized models?
06:44 Maya: we recommend evaluation sets and Redwood Optimize to monitor quality regressions. Small regressions can happen; we can quantify via evals and keep fallbacks to higher-quality variants if a regression breaches thresholds.
06:57 Liam: what about data residency costs? if we require EU-only regions does that change pricing?
07:02 Jon: pricing varies a bit by region; EU region GPUs often cost more. We'll include region multipliers in the TCO.
07:10 Nora: encryption at rest—in hosted do we have customer-managed keys?
07:14 Maya: hosted supports CMEK in supported clouds, private gives full HSM options. We'll need to show architecture diagrams.
07:21 Priya: can Redwood provide an estimate for a 3-month pilot with 250k tokens/day ramping to 2M? We need both hosted and dedicated figures.
07:29 Evelyn: yes — we'll model both. We'll need a sample traffic CSV and your target SLOs. Also confirm if you want reserved pool sizing for peak or average.
07:40 Samir: we probably want to commit to baseline average and allow for burst credits.
07:45 Liam: on invoicing — can we get monthly caps and alerts?
07:49 Jon: yes, billing caps + alerts + token-level reporting in the console.
07:54 Priya: one more technical: do you support prefix cache TTL and cache invalidation? If our prompts sometimes include PII, we need TTL controls.
08:03 Maya: yes TTL and scoping controls; you can mark cacheable vs non-cacheable inputs. PII should be expressly excluded. We'll also highlight data retention controls.
08:16 Samir: let's roleplay the pilot: 6-week pilot, hosted first 2 weeks to iterate, then run dedicated benchmark week and compare unit cost. Does that make sense?
08:26 Evelyn: totally standard. We'll propose a pilot SOW with milestones and success criteria (latency, cost per token, feature coverage).
08:33 Liam: success criteria from Finance: under $X per effective token — we'll fill X after running baseline. Also show break-even month where dedicated wins.
08:42 Nora: Security success: KMS integration test and audit log ingestion working.
08:47 Maya: technical note — for your long synths we can enable streaming and partial generation which reduces lock-step latency and perceived latency for users. That sometimes interacts with prefix caching; we'll document best practices.
08:59 Priya: how granular is model version pinning? we want to lock to a version during pilot, not float to new weights.
09:05 Jon: you can pin model versions and rollout via canary/A-B, Redwood supports rollbacks and automatic fallback to previous pinned version.
09:13 Samir: good. Any red flags we should be aware of?
09:16 Maya: maybe three: 1) If you commit too small a dedicated pool you may get high overage charges during burst; 2) quantization can cause subtle quality loss, need eval sets; 3) VPC/on-prem networking usually needs a short lead time for firewall and identity setup.
09:32 Priya: understood. Can you also send sample kb-arrays or perf numbers for our model family choices?
09:37 Maya: yes, we'll attach a model perf matrix and the TCO spreadsheet.
09:41 Liam: perfect. On the pricing spreadsheet, please include amortized amortization for reserved GPU months and an example showing effective cost per 1k tokens under several scenarios.
09:52 Evelyn: will do. We'll include scenario A (hosted only), B (hybrid routing), C (dedicated reserved + burst).
09:59 Samir: ok, next steps again?
10:01 Evelyn: I'll recap in the follow-up email. High level: we build pilot SOW and TCO, Maya will run technical deep dive for VPC/KMS with Nora, Hydra provides traffic CSV and SLOs.
10:12 Priya: can we lock the technical deep dive for week of Sep 6?
10:15 Maya: yes I'll send invites.
10:17 Jon: I'll also add a short checklist for firewall rules and quotas.
10:20 Liam: fine. That covers most. Thanks.
10:23 Samir: thanks everyone.

END TRANSCRIPT

NOTES: Shared artifacts mentioned: hosted_vs_dedicated_TCO.xlsx (link to be provided in follow-up), model_perf_matrix.pdf. There is moderate transcription noise on some acronyms (e.g., HSM heard as "H-S-M"), and a few speaker labels merged (some lines may be generic).
